[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"GitOps and Continuous Delivery in Kubernetes with ArgoCD and Flux"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitOps is an operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development--such as version control, collaboration, compliance, and CI/CD--and applies them to infrastructure automation. In a Kubernetes environment, GitOps uses Git as the single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A running Kubernetes cluster (v1.22+ recommended)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"kubectl configured to communicate with your cluster."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A dedicated GitHub or GitLab repository to store your Kubernetes manifests."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing ArgoCD"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"ArgoCD is a declarative, GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes. First, create a dedicated namespace for ArgoCD and apply the official installation manifest."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"kubectl create namespace argocd
kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the pods are running, you can access the ArgoCD API server. For local testing, port-forward the service to your local machine."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Deploying an Application with ArgoCD"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"ArgoCD uses an Application Custom Resource Definition (CRD) to monitor the state of your Git repository and sync it with the cluster. Below is an example application manifest."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: guestbook
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/argoproj/argocd-example-apps.git
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: guestbook
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: default
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing and Configuring Flux v2"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Flux is another prominent GitOps tool tailored for Kubernetes, structured as a set of specialized controllers. To install Flux, use the official command-line interface."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"flux check --pre
flux bootstrap github \
  --owner=<YOUR-GITHUB-USER> \
  --repository=<YOUR-REPO-NAME> \
  --branch=main \
  --path=clusters/my-cluster \
  --personal"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Defining a Flux GitRepository and Kustomization"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Flux relies on custom resources like GitRepository and Kustomization to reconcile cluster state. Create a file named sync.yaml with the following configurations:"},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: podinfo
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
    interval: 1m
    url: https://github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo
    ref:
      branch: master
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: podinfo
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 5m
  targetNamespace: default
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: podinfo
  path: ./kustomize
  prune: true"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion and Best Practices"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both ArgoCD and Flux provide robust GitOps workflows for Kubernetes. Choose ArgoCD if you require a rich Web UI and multi-cluster management out of the box. Choose Flux if you prefer a lightweight, controller-first approach natively integrated with Kubernetes Custom Resources."}]
